### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via safeParse (symbol, a method of interface SafeParseable))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), registerFlow (literal, a string literal in FLOW_REGISTRATION_TODO_ID; a string literal in a comment in ConversionTodoNotice; a string literal in a comment in StoredFlowCanonicalization; a string literal in a comment in canonicalizeStoredFlow))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), registerFlow (literal, a string literal in FLOW_REGISTRATION_TODO_ID; a string literal in a comment in ConversionTodoNotice; a string literal in a comment in StoredFlowCanonicalization; a string literal in a comment in canonicalizeStoredFlow))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), registerFlow (literal, a string literal in FLOW_REGISTRATION_TODO_ID; a string literal in a comment in ConversionTodoNotice; a string literal in a comment in StoredFlowCanonicalization; a string literal in a comment in canonicalizeStoredFlow))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), IAutomationService (symbol, a top-level interface), registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), registerFlow (literal, a string literal in FLOW_REGISTRATION_TODO_ID; a string literal in a comment in ConversionTodoNotice; a string literal in a comment in StoredFlowCanonicalization; a string literal in a comment in canonicalizeStoredFlow))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), registerFlow (literal, a string literal in FLOW_REGISTRATION_TODO_ID; a string literal in a comment in ConversionTodoNotice; a string literal in a comment in StoredFlowCanonicalization; a string literal in a comment in canonicalizeStoredFlow))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), safeParse (symbol, a method of interface SafeParseable), registerFlow (literal, a string literal in FLOW_REGISTRATION_TODO_ID; a string literal in a comment in ConversionTodoNotice; a string literal in a comment in StoredFlowCanonicalization; a string literal in a comment in canonicalizeStoredFlow))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via IAutomationService (symbol, a top-level interface), registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), registerFlow (literal, a string literal in FLOW_REGISTRATION_TODO_ID; a string literal in a comment in ConversionTodoNotice; a string literal in a comment in StoredFlowCanonicalization; a string literal in a comment in canonicalizeStoredFlow))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `safeParse (5 routes)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 228357ab69aaaaba6e306b7cce7bb3fdc757ccb7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bfb9b4451dd7af3fe7c4c9b9eda85bbe86fcdbce` — the merge of head `ac768f1d54f1225d9cb6e64b581ca0fe8312774d` into base `228357ab69aaaaba6e306b7cce7bb3fdc757ccb7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bfb9b4451dd7af3fe7c4c9b9eda85bbe86fcdbce && git checkout bfb9b4451dd7af3fe7c4c9b9eda85bbe86fcdbce
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 228357ab69aaaaba6e306b7cce7bb3fdc757ccb7 ac768f1d54f1225d9cb6e64b581ca0fe8312774d && git checkout -B drift-repro 228357ab69aaaaba6e306b7cce7bb3fdc757ccb7 && git merge --no-ff ac768f1d54f1225d9cb6e64b581ca0fe8312774d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 228357ab69aaaaba6e306b7cce7bb3fdc757ccb7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 228357ab69aaaaba6e306b7cce7bb3fdc757ccb7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ac768f1d54f1225d9cb6e64b581ca0fe8312774d`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23317 with every comment (triage `6152829172`, the unlock `6155083387`, the claim `6156647772`, the serial note `6157679610`, report `6158463913`, ACCEPT `6158509652`); PR #23356 body, its one bot comment, the 13-file list and the net diff `origin/main...ac768f1d5` (+834 / -125, identical to the file list); PR #23315 (merged `572ecfb2e`) with records `6152721854` and `6154280528` and its changeset `.changeset/23269-v18-stored-row-fates.md`; PR #23319 (#23260, merged `ca0bdbcca`); `origin/main` for `engine.ts` (the four checks, `registerFlow`, `deriveTriggerBinding`), `plugin.ts` (`holdsFlowDefinition`), `protocol.ts` (the save door at 21889, the stored pass at 22936 to 23010, the rehydration read at 6455 to 6510, the two other canonicalize seams at 25965 and 26212), `stored-migration.ts` (the report lines), `conversions/walk.ts`, `conversions/refused-shapes.ts`, `conversions/types.ts`, `ui/component.zod.ts` (`ComponentPropsMap`), `shared/lazy-schema.ts`, `ui/page.zod.ts`, `automation/control-flow.zod.ts` (`FlowGraph`, `collectFlowGraphs`), `lint/src/validate-component-props.ts` and `authoring-rules.ts`, `runtime/tsup.config.ts`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, the spec lane's Clause-② line; the #23316 branch at `2b84fe555` (`git diff origin/main...`, 22 files) for `engine.ts`, `plugin.ts` and `contracts/automation-service.ts`; the head's check-runs (four polls, 01:0xZ to 01:14Z).

**Check-runs on the head at 01:14Z: 39 runs, 31 success, 5 skipped, 0 failed, 4 `in_progress`: Test Core 3 to 6.** `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, Test Core 1/6 and 2/6 and the claim guards are green. The four open shards are reported, not assumed: this record judges the contract, and the landing condition (every check green) is the owning seat's to read once they finish.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong.

1. **`registerFlow` refuses exactly what it refused on `main`, with byte-identical messages, in the same order: RIGHT.** Read check by check against `origin/main`. `validateNodeConfigKeys`: the per-key line is the same template (`node 'ID' (TYPE): unknown config key ... Declared here: ...`), now carried as `UndeclaredConfigKey.line`, scoped with the same `graph.scope · ` prefix, pushed per node in the same node-then-key order the old `scoped` list transferred in, under the same `Flow 'NAME' rejected: N undeclared config key(s).` head and tail. `validateDecisionModes`: `  • ${at}node 'ID' (decision) at config.mode: ${issue.message}` and the same head. `validateFlowExpressions`: every `failures.push` became `refuse(path, where, message, source)`, whose line is `  • ${where}: ${message}\n      source: \`${source}\`` with the same `where` strings and the same raw `source` values (`e.source`, `slot.source`, `refusal.source`, `shapeRefusal.source`, `blankRefusal.source`); the head sentence is unchanged. `validateApiTriggerSecret`: `Flow 'NAME' rejected: ${why}` where `why` is the old literal from `it binds the inbound` onward. `registerFlow` iterates `registrationChecks({ advisory: true })` in the old order (keys, modes, expressions, secret) and throws `new Error(refusal.message)`, a plain `Error` without `code`, as each check threw before. A check that throws rather than refuses still propagates out of `registerFlow` unchanged (the loop does not catch). Nothing after the checks moves: the only other `registerFlow` hunk swaps `this.canonicalizeStoredFlow` for `this.canonicalizeFlow`, whose body is the old method's body verbatim (the hunk inserts the signature above an unchanged `// ADR-0087 D2 — the runtime load seam` block), so the chain run, parse, cycle check and region validation registration does are what they were.
   - **The `advisory` flag: RIGHT, and it moves no refusal in either direction.** On `main` the schema-aware pass inside `check()` only calls `this.logger.warn` (#1928, logged never thrown); it pushes nothing to `failures`. `advisory: true` (registration) keeps that logging; `advisory: false` (the stored pass) skips only the `logger.warn` block. No check that threw at registration now only warns, and nothing that warned now throws. Pinned: the stored pass logs nothing while `registerFlow` warns on the same flow (a start-node condition naming the misspelled field `amout`).
   - **The pins.** The two-direction corpus pin (seventeen flows, listed exactly when `registerFlow` throws), the first-refusal-wins pin and the eight per-case pins hold the refusal SET and the ORDER. The per-case message pins match a regex fragment of the check's words, not the whole string, so byte-identity rests on the diff reading above rather than on a pin. Strong enough for the card's hard line, with that caveat named.

2. **No door moves: RIGHT.** `FlowSchema`, `ViewDataSchema`, `PageSchema`, `ObjectSchema` and the component-props gate are untouched. The three doors that canonicalize without registering read only `conflicts`, `storable` and `parsed` off the result (`protocol.ts` 21905 to 21925, 25965 to 25983, 26212 to 26217; `plugin.ts:352`), so the lazy `todos` accessor never runs there; pinned with a spy. The rehydration read (`convertStoredItem`, `protocol.ts:6455`) warns on notices and discards TODOs, so a stored page carrying the binding gains no boot log line. `deriveTriggerBinding`, which the stored pass now runs, has no logger call. The stored pass keeps `storedMigrationClean` and `--apply` writes nothing (pinned on a page row and on the flow rows). One published-shape subtlety, cost only: `todos` is an enumerable accessor on the returned literal, so a caller that spreads or `JSON.stringify`s the whole result would run the four checks; none on `main` does, and the accessor never throws (`registrationCheckRefusals` catches).

3. **Item 1, the detector is the door's own judge, keyed by the entry id, headers withheld: RIGHT.** `componentApiBindingRefusal` first takes `apiBindingRefusal(data)` (`ViewDataSchema.safeParse`, the view judge PR #23315 landed), then parses the same `data` with the component's OWN `ComponentPropsMap[type].shape.data` member, the schema the component-props gate parses, and lists the site only when that member's issues carry the identical prescription string. `lazySchema` is a Proxy that forwards `.shape` to the real instance (`shared/lazy-schema.ts`), so the lookup resolves on the four lazy rows. The listing rides the existing `viewDataApiProvider` detector, so the TODO's `conversionId` is `view-data-api-provider-retired`; `from` goes through `describeApiBinding`, which keeps only `provider` and each request block's `url` and `method` (`[withheld]` otherwise), pinned on a `Bearer` header. Reach: `mapPageComponents` walks `regions[].components`, `slots` (one component or a list) and every `pageComponentSlotPositions()` container, panel lists included; the nested-tabs and slot paths pinned are the walker's own spellings.
   - **The four components are exactly the rows whose `data` is `ViewDataSchema`: RIGHT.** `component.zod.ts` on `main` carries exactly four `data: ViewDataSchema.optional()` members, at 6027 (`ObjectGridPropsSchema`), 8979 (`ObjectMapPropsSchema`), 9529 (`ObjectGanttPropsSchema`) and 10105 (`ObjectTreePropsSchema`). `object-kanban` / `object-calendar` / `object-timeline` take a row array under `data` and refuse the binding for its shape, with a different message, so the equality judge leaves them out, and the door-agreement pin iterates every `ComponentPropsMap` key in both directions.
   - **The D3 entry's new scope text is TRUE, the fate sentence included.** `PageComponent.properties` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (`page.zod.ts:592`), so `PageSchema` accepts the page; the props rule is `surfaces: CLI_ONLY` with `commands: ALL` (`authoring-rules.ts:1170-1193`; its own header at `validate-component-props.ts:111-116` names the three CLI doors and says the runtime publish door does not run it). So "the page still loads and saves, while `os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` refuse the binding in source" is what the code does; the `acceptanceCriteria`, `surface` and `replacement` sentences name the same four components and the same gate.

4. **Item 2, the stored pass lists exactly `registerFlow`'s refusals, from one list, deduped by site: RIGHT.** `registrationChecks` is the one ordered list; `registerFlow` throws its first refusal and `registrationCheckRefusals` collects all of them with `advisory: false`, so a check added to the list is refused and previewed alike (the comment at the call site says so). Site paths are spelled as the conversion walk spells them: `storedGraphPath` renders `FlowGraph.path` (`['nodes', 1, 'config', 'body']`) as `flows[0].nodes[1].config.body`, and `mapFlowNodeList` on `main` spells a nested node `${path}.config.${key}.nodes[i]` and a branch `${path}.config.${key}[i].nodes[j]`, so the two agree at depth. The dedupe keys on that path against the chain's TODOs; the one overlap that exists today is the value-slot site (D3 `flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused` and `validateFlowExpressions`), pinned as one line under the D3 id, and the existing #23269 "exactly one TODO" engine pin stays green only with the skip (ablation A4).
   - **#23260's value arm (unlock `6155083387`): COVERED, and the operator is told.** PR #23319 put the arm inside `flowNodeConfigRefusals`, which `FlowSchema`'s superRefine runs, so `get_record` `limit: '{x}'` is refused by the parse, before any registration check. `canonicalizeFlow` throws it, `canonicalizeStoredFlow` throws it (pinned beside `registerFlow` on `/limit/`), and the stored pass's existing catch (`protocol.ts:22949-22960`) records the row `failed` with `the flow does not canonicalize: ` plus the parse's message, which `formatStoredMigrationReport` prints under `✗ N row(s) could not be rewritten`. Not a TODO, and not silence: a `failed` row keeps `storedMigrationClean` false. The changeset and `cli.mdx` say exactly this.
   - Two residuals, noted not failed. (a) The site index is taken over `graph.nodes`, the list `collectFlowGraphs` hands out after dropping a non-record member, while `FlowGraph.path` indexes the raw list; they differ only for a region with a dropped member, which the region validator refuses inside `canonicalizeFlow` before the checks run, so no listed path is reachable off by one. (b) The dedupe is by path across ids: a future chain TODO at a site a registration check also refuses would keep the chain's line and drop the `registerFlow` one. One line per site is the chosen policy; today the only such site is the value slot, where the chain's line is the retirement's own.

5. **`@objectstack/spec` public surface: no export name changes, two published-output widenings, both declared: RIGHT.** `refused-shapes.ts`'s new helper is module-private; `conversions/index.ts` and `ui/index.ts` are untouched (`check:api-surface` green, nothing regenerated). `ConversionTodoNotice.conversionId` may now be `'registerFlow'`: declared in its docblock (`conversions/types.ts`). `IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow(...).todos?` now also carries registration refusals: declared in the member's docblock and the `@returns` line (`contracts/automation-service.ts`). `ApplyConversionsOptions.onTodo` now also receives a page-component TODO under the D3 id: named in the changeset, the same declaration route record `6152721854` ① item 5 accepted. No `#NNNN` reaches a runtime string: the citations sit in TSDoc, and the TODO prose carries none.

6. **`@objectstack/service-automation` public surface: one widening, declared; one new module export kept off the index: RIGHT.** `AutomationEngine.canonicalizeStoredFlow(...).todos` (an exported class's published return) now also carries registration refusals; the method's docblock says so, and the changeset names it. `FLOW_REGISTRATION_TODO_ID` is a named export of `engine.ts` only: `src/index.ts` re-exports `engine.js` by name (lines 4 and 70 to 88) and is not in the diff, so the constant is not barrel-reachable. The internal types `RegistrationCheckSite` / `RegistrationCheckRefusal` are not exported.

7. **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: docblocks only, and the restated domain is declared: RIGHT.** No code in the package changes. `StoredMigrationTodo.conversionId`'s docblock now says what the field has carried since PR #23315 (a D3 id) plus `registerFlow`, and `StoredFlowCanonicalization.todos?` restates the contract member it mirrors. The flattening at `protocol.ts:23006-23014` is unchanged and reads `flowResult.todos ?? []`, a contract-declared optional (record `6154280528` ① item 1). The widened domain reaches this package's published report rows through the carrier in `@objectstack/spec`, which the changeset names; the docblock is the declaration on this side, and with no feature, improvement or fix in the package's own code no version line is owed here. See ②.

8. **`@objectstack/runtime`: the ledger row is non-shipping: RIGHT.** `dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` is read by `scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs` (its `DECLARATION` constant) and by one conformance test; `tsup.config.ts`'s entry is `src/index.ts`, and the only reference under `src/` is a comment in `http-dispatcher.ts`. The row is right in substance: the engine's `flowRegistrationTodo` stamps `code: CONVERSION_TODO_CODE` (`OS_METADATA_CONVERSION_TODO`) on a returned record, never on a throw (`registerFlow` throws its own plain refusal), which is the `foreign-vocabulary` verdict the sibling `apply.ts` row carries. `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on the head.

9. **`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, the two `--stored` rows: TRUE now.** `formatStoredMigrationReport` prints `TODO ${conversionId}: ${from} left as stored at ${path} — ${reason}` (`stored-migration.ts:456`), so a registration site prints as `TODO registerFlow: ...` with the fate sentence leading; a parse refusal prints under the `could not be rewritten` block; the page fate matches item 3; the old row's "the parse or the boot refuses the row" would have been false for a page, and the edit removes that sentence for the page case only.

10. **The one changed test that called the private validator: RIGHT.** `config-unknown-keys.test.ts` pinned "builtin types judged by the spec are not walked; a plugin type is". The subject's signature changed from throw to return, and the pin now asserts `undefined` for the builtin set and a returned `message` matching `/undeclared config key/` for the plugin type, the same two facts in the new shape. No assertion was weakened.

11. **Serial with #23316 (`2b84fe555`): no semantic collision visible from the two diffs.** Contract: #23316 adds `getFlowRegistration?(name)` at line 1001 with a `FlowRegistration` type import; this PR edits the `canonicalizeStoredFlow` docblock at 802 to 820; different members, no shared line. Engine: #23316 adds a `flowRefusals` map, deletes the name from it after `this.flows.set(name, parsed)` (a line after the checks, which this PR does not touch), deletes it in `withdrawFlow`, and adds `recordFlowRefusal` / `getFlowRegistration`; this PR's engine hunks are the check calls, the two canonicalize methods, the four checks and the new helpers. The one semantic seam is `recordFlowRefusal` keeping what `registerFlow` threw (`message`, and `code` only when the thrown error carries a string one): this PR keeps the message byte-identical and still throws a plain `Error` without `code`, so a recorded refusal reads the same after either merge order. #23316 imports `FlowRegistrationRefusal` from `@objectstack/spec/api`; this PR's `RegistrationCheckRefusal` is a different, unexported name. #23316 regenerates `packages/spec/api-surface/*.json`; this PR touches none of those. The joint typecheck is not measured here either; the second PR to queue merges `main`, and the queue's own `Type Check · workspace` is the measurement.

### ② Semver level

**The changeset `.changeset/23317-stored-preview-gaps.md` (`minor` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-automation`; `Clause-②: yes (widening: ...)`) matches what the diff publishes. PASS.**

- `@objectstack/spec`: `minor`. RIGHT: a published contract member's output widens (`IAutomationService.canonicalizeStoredFlow(...).todos?` now also carries registration refusals) and the published `ConversionTodoNotice.conversionId` domain widens by `'registerFlow'`. Precedent: record `6152721854` ② and `6154280528` ② put `todos?` and the `conversionId` domain widening on `minor` for this package; `.changeset/23158-ai-store-caller-context.md` for an additive member on a published contract method.
- `@objectstack/service-automation`: `minor`. RIGHT: `AutomationEngine.canonicalizeStoredFlow(...).todos` on an exported class's published return now carries more (the method entered as a 17.0.0 Minor Change; precedents `.changeset/23178-settings-auth-gate.md`, `.changeset/pre/15195-plugin-auth-default-organization-boot-invariant.md`, and PR #23315's own line for the same member).
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: no line, and none owed. Its code is unchanged (docblocks only); the widened domain of `StoredMigrationTodo.conversionId` arrives through the spec carrier the changeset names and is declared in the field's docblock. The stricter reading of `6152721854` ① item 5 would also name this package; that record's `minor` for it rode a type addition (`StoredFlowCanonicalization.todos?`), which this PR does not repeat. Not a FAIL carrier.
- `@objectstack/runtime`: no line, and none owed (① item 8).
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: RIGHT**, on PR body line 2 and the changeset's long spelling (`readClause2Line` takes the arm as the first token inside the parenthesis: value `yes`, arm `widening`, as `6154280528` ② measured). The arm is right: nothing narrows, no door accepts or refuses anything it did not before (① items 1 to 4), nothing authorable is removed or renamed, so no breaking marker, no FROM to TO text and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. Triage's and the claim's `no` was the prediction; the diff is the fact, and the dev flipped it on the diff, which is the direction `landing-operations.md` wants (a wrong `no` is the auditable false declaration, a flipped `yes` on a measured widening is not).
- `skip-changeset` does not apply; both named packages publish. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (`check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration`) are green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every deviation and every `out_of_scope_findings` entry in report `6158463913`, answered or escalated.

- **Deviation 1, `Clause-②` flipped to `yes (widening)`:** answered in ②: right, and the three members it names are exactly the ones the diff publishes (① items 5 and 6).
- **Deviation 2, file surface beyond the claim:** each forced by the diff and right. The runtime ledger row (① item 8) is what `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` demands of a new `OS_METADATA_CONVERSION_TODO` stamp and ships nothing; the two spec docblocks are the declarations ② requires; the `cli.mdx` row would otherwise have become false (① item 9); the private-validator test followed its subject's signature (① item 10); the protocol test is a pin on the report channel. `protocol.ts` untouched, as fenced for PR #23345.
